title: 1 in 3 People Globally Can't Afford a Healthy Diet — UN
paragraphs: About one in three people around the world cannot afford a healthy diet, according to a major new report by the United Nations.

The report, called The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026, was released on July 21, 2026, by five UN agencies: the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), UNICEF, the World Food Programme (WFP) and the World Health Organization (WHO).

According to the report, 2.69 billion people, or 32.7% of the world's population, were unable to afford a healthy diet in 2025. This was an improvement compared with 2021, when the figure was 2.97 billion, or 37.4% of the population. However, the cost of a healthy diet has continued to rise. In 2025, it reached an average of 4.28 dollars per person per day, adjusted for differences in prices between countries, up from 3.44 dollars in 2021.

The situation varies greatly between regions. In Africa, the problem has become worse, with 66.6% of people unable to afford a healthy diet. This is more than twice the proportion in Asia and in Latin America and the Caribbean. The report found that most of the price that consumers pay for food comes from activities that take place after food leaves the farm, such as processing, transport and selling.
There was some good news. Global hunger fell for the third year in a row. In 2025, about 645 million people, or 7.8% of the world's population, faced hunger, down from 8.1% in 2024.

However, progress on nutrition has been slow. About 150 million children under the age of five are too short for their age, a sign of poor nutrition. Only 30.8% of young children aged six to 23 months eat a diet with enough variety. At the same time, adult obesity has risen from 12.1% in 2012 to 16.2% in 2024, and anemia among women is getting worse.

According to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, a healthy diet remains unaffordable for one in three people around the world. The agencies have called on governments to increase the supply of nutritious food, reduce costs and make healthy food the easy choice.
